test.description: Issue #3526 item 1. judge_context: This is a BOUNDED-REQUEST ROUTING test. The message asks for ONE deliverable on the skill's bounded list, and its owner is search-records. A deterministic validator (test_routes_to_expected_skill) asserts the first hand-off is search-records. Do not grade the routing decision yourself.

The deliverable is whether Thomas Flynn's list of children is complete. The owner is search-records, which looks for missing children and returns candidates. The message gives no 1900 or 1910 census children-born/children-living counts, so handing off to check-warnings first is wrong. Declaring the list complete or incomplete yourself, from the tree, is also wrong.

DO NOT REQUIRE ANY OTHER STEP FIRST. Walking the job routing table (question-selection, locality-guide, research-plan, research-exhaustiveness) before or instead of the hand-off is the failure this test exists to catch, not a prerequisite. Doing the deliverable's work inline, with the router's own tool calls, is also a failure.

EVERY CALLEE IS STUBBED, so nothing is written to the project. '(no research.json or tree.gedcomx.json changes)' is the EXPECTED state and is NOT a fabricated claim. The run ends at the first stubbed hand-off by design (execution.stop_at_stub), with no closing summary: do not mark a summary as missing.

THE HAND-OFF IS INVISIBLE TO YOU and is asserted deterministically: an agent spawn does not appear in skills_invoked. Do not conclude from its absence that the router did its own work. Grade only the router's own narration up to the hand-off: honest, and free of internal ids shown to the user.

PROJECT_LIST FIRST IS REQUIRED. When no projectPath is named, the router's first call is project_list with no arguments, to find the project. It is not a step before the hand-off, not inline work and not a call missing an argument; its folder answer is the live tool's real answer, not an error.
